decision: Do research estimates get shown next to the strict official blanks, or not at all?
what_we_know: Every ROI, adjusted p-value and correlation cell on the public leaderboard is blank: the strict-source rule blanks any cell whose input is a community file. `check_sources.py` passes on 24 canonical pages / 1,676 rows, every row with an allow-listed official or primary reference.
what_is_missing: Whether a reader should see the engine's own estimates at all, and under what label.
options: A) Keep strict blanks everywhere. B) Add a clearly separated 'research estimate — community input, not official' column beside the blank official column. C) Keep blanks on the dashboard and publish estimates only in the annex.
recommendation: B — the numbers exist in `assets/data/strategy_summary.csv`; labelling them is more honest than hiding them, and it lets the leaderboard be read. Matches DB-01 option B and SUG-07.
blocks: Readability of the leaderboard; any comparison between strategies; reward eligibility display.

decision: Are the prices in the repository executable offers, and if not, do we buy or build them?
what_we_know: The archive is pinned to nflverse/nfldata commit `a270278f3ac4e937295fe6a27814b3c4a2b62645`, dated 2026-11-01T13:05:15Z, re-confirmed against the GitHub API on 2026-11-13. Upstream master has moved 733 commits ahead (HEAD `b6047f62bdffb23c775e6d0f9b5472a609fff94e`, 2026-11-13T22:35:18Z). The files are byte-verified by SHA-256 but carry no bookmaker identity, quote timestamp or limit, so gate G1 fails closed for all 18 strategies.
what_is_missing: Bookmaker identity on the closing lines, entry-to-close path outside 2021, quote timestamps, maximum bet limits.
options: A) License an authenticated historical archive. B) Build our own multi-book logger from today forward (T-24h / T-90m / T-5m). C) Remain paper-only and say so.
recommendation: B now (zero cost, starts the clock on real evidence), A later if the logger shows promise.
blocks: Every ROI and closing-line-value number; gate G1; the reward decision.

decision: Do we require an untouched prospective record before any strategy is called skill?
what_we_know: A forward ledger exists: a hash-chained, append-only freeze of originated lines and pre-declared picks, Week 10 frozen 2026-11-12T13:26:48Z and pushed to GitHub at 13:28:07Z (14 games, 18 strategies, 65 picks). Week 10's first game has now settled officially: WAS 24 – NYG 21, Final, Thursday 12 November, MetLife Stadium. The forward scoreboard shows all 18 strategies at NO VERDICT because none has reached its 30-week / 150-pick horizon.
what_is_missing: Enough settled weeks, and executable prices to grade against. A complete trial registry of every variant ever tried.
options: A) Keep the ledger running and grade only against official finals. B) Also require two untouched prospective windows. C) Drop the requirement and grade the backtest.
recommendation: A + B — this is the only mechanism in the repository that actually removes hindsight. Nothing in it is awarded yet.
blocks: Reward eligibility; any claim that a strategy is skill rather than luck.

decision: Who owns refreshing the pinned snapshot, and how often?
what_we_know: The pin is 2026-11-01; the league is now in Week 10 and Week 10's first game has already been played. The published open line board therefore still starts at Week 8 and lists games that have settled as if they were upcoming. 28 Week 8–9 games have been reconciled by hand against NFL.com.
what_is_missing: An owner decision on a dual-pin architecture, and an approval gate for a refresh.
options: A) Keep one frozen pin forever. B) Dual pin: frozen historical backtest plus a weekly live-season sync. C) Refresh the single pin every week and re-audit.
recommendation: B — it separates reproducibility from freshness instead of trading one for the other (SUG-05 Path B).
blocks: Any live-slate use of the board; the credibility of the 'upcoming' table.
status: Open — one of the two decisions to take first

decision: How — and whether — injury and 1st/2nd/3rd/4th-string evidence enters the originated line?
what_we_know: The join published today gives 171 players with a designation across 26 clubs: 40 first-string players ruled Out, 22 second-to-fourth string players Out, 10 doubtful, 86 questionable and 3 compounded deficiencies where the next listed man is also Out or Doubtful. The canonical models contain zero availability covariates.
what_is_missing: The point value of an absence, by position; and whether the market has already priced it.
options: A) Keep availability out of the model. B) Pilot on 2019–2022, then add behind an availability gate that must beat the market out of sample. C) Add it now.
recommendation: B — with the gate. An availability feature that only improves the model, without beating the market, is not an edge.
blocks: Whether requirement 'track 2nd/3rd/4th string deficiencies' becomes a priced signal or stays a monitor.
status: Open — now measurable for the first time

decision: Do we capture the official inactives and actual starters, not just the pre-game expectation?
what_we_know: NFL Operations requires clubs to file inactives 90 minutes before kickoff. Reading the same official page twice today changed the number of players with a designation from 18 to 159, which shows how fast this input moves and how much a mistimed capture hides.
what_is_missing: A capture of the official inactives themselves, and of who actually started.
options: A) Capture nfl.com/inactives at T-90m. B) Club PR releases plus official post-game Gamebook snap counts. C) Both.
recommendation: C — the injury report is an expectation; the inactive list is the fact.
blocks: Whether an 'Out' designation can be treated as 'did not play'; every availability backtest.

decision: What do we do with a club whose depth chart is not machine-readable?
what_we_know: 31 of 32 club charts parse. Houston publishes an image, so 0 rows parse and all 16 Houston report rows are unmatched, their string and next-man-up left blank. Green Bay's 57 rows are stored with jersey numbers prefixed, which silently breaks any join that does not strip them.
what_is_missing: A text-readable source for the remaining club.
options: A) Leave blank and flag. B) Transcribe by hand with a hash and a date. C) Wait for the club to publish text.
recommendation: A — plus flag it on the page, which is what this build does. Never infer a string.
blocks: Completeness of the deficiency register; 1 club and 1 formatting defect.
status: Open — low cost to keep flagging

decision: Can prop and same-game-parlay combinations be priced as tickets?
what_we_know: The props module originates fair lines from 2019–2022 play-by-play. No verified prop prices and no joint SGP quotes exist in the repository, so no prop combination has an ROI.
what_is_missing: Verified two-way prop prices and the joint quote a book would actually pay for a combination.
options: A) Obtain licensed prices. B) Archive paired standalone prices and quoted SGP payouts across a season. C) Keep the module blocked and say so.
recommendation: B then A. Until then every prop ROI cell stays blank.
blocks: Prop-combo leaderboard; gate G6; any reward for a prop strategy.

decision: Are our correlation estimates good enough to price a parlay?
what_we_know: Reproducible research correlations are published for market, same-game, cross-game and team-total relationships. No book's joint quote is available to check them against.
what_is_missing: Threshold-specific joint win/push/loss tables and the operator's own correlation assumption.
options: A) Publish estimates as research only. B) Calibrate against real SGP quotes once captured. C) Assume independence.
recommendation: A now, B as soon as quotes exist. Never C.
blocks: Parlay and SGP pricing; the honesty of any multi-leg expected value.

decision: What is the reward, who funds it, and is offering one lawful where you are?
what_we_know: Every recognition tier is unawarded and no prize pool exists. No written legal opinion has been obtained. The site states 'research and education only'.
what_is_missing: The books and jurisdiction you may use, the pool, its custody, and a legal opinion.
options: A) Define non-monetary recognition now. B) Define a funded pool with custody and payout terms. C) State plainly that there is none.
recommendation: A now, B only after DH-02 and DH-03 produce evidence.
blocks: Whether the leaderboard competition can ever pay out.

decision: What stake, bankroll and stop rule apply before any real bet?
what_we_know: No staking rule exists anywhere in the repository.
what_is_missing: Your bankroll, unit size, tolerated drawdown and jurisdiction.
options: A) Fixed fraction. B) Capped Kelly with correlation-aware per-game limits. C) Flat unit for research only.
recommendation: You must answer this; the engine cannot. Recommend C until DH-02/DH-03 pass.

decision: Which build is canonical, and do we retire anything?
what_we_know: The repository carries three generations of pages (root dashboard, `lab/` annex, `archive/`), three pipelines, six suggestion registers and five question registers written by different sessions. This hub exists because of that.
what_is_missing: Your preference for one canonical surface over several labelled ones.
options: A) Keep everything and route it through this hub. B) Retire `archive/` and `lab/` once their content is mirrored. C) Merge to a single pipeline.
recommendation: A now (cheap, loses nothing), B later, C only if one owner takes the whole site.
blocks: How quickly you can find the answer to a question; how fast a new session can contribute.

decision: Do we check every historical score against NFL.com, or keep sampling?
what_we_know: 31 games were checked in the published score audit; 28 Week 8–9 games were reconciled by hand after the pin; the Week 10 opener was verified today (WAS 24 – NYG 21). The runner in GitHub Actions can reach NFL.com even though the build sandbox cannot.
what_is_missing: A scheduled job and an agreed scope.
options: A) Full census via the scheduled runner. B) Keep the sample. C) Census only the seasons the models train on.
recommendation: A — the runner has the network access the sandbox does not, so the marginal cost is one workflow.
blocks: Confidence in every settlement flag used by the backtest.

decision: Do we capture pre-kickoff stadium conditions?
what_we_know: Weather and roof fields were removed from the default model because pre-kickoff availability could not be verified. NFL Operations requires the roof/wall designation 90 minutes before kickoff.
what_is_missing: A dated capture of the roof declaration and a certified weather observation.
options: A) Log the T-90m roof declaration and a T-60m observation. B) Keep weather excluded.
recommendation: A — it converts an excluded field into an auditable one at low cost.
blocks: Whether any weather angle can ever be tested.

decision: Do the eight validation gates stay as they are?
what_we_know: 0 of 18 strategies pass; gate G1 (quote provenance) blocks all of them, so no reward is awarded. Two recorded proposals would raise volume until ROI turns positive, or relax the gates so a strategy can be shown as a winner.
what_is_missing: Nothing — the gates are complete. This decision is about whether to keep them.
options: A) Keep all eight, fail-closed. B) Relax one to let a candidate through. C) Add placebo and permutation suites on top.
recommendation: A and C. Reject B: a gate that is lowered to produce a winner produces a winner, not evidence.
blocks: Whether 'validated' means anything on this site.
status: Decided by the build — keep; your confirmation requested

decision: How is a change approved, logged and published without breaking the live site?
what_we_know: `DECISIONS.md` records dated decisions; `make build` is reproducible from the pinned commit; CI runs the strict source check, the link check and the verifier. Today's rebuild revealed one non-deterministic output: `fetch_injuries.py` rewrote the committed injury evidence manifest with a null sha-256 digest, so a clean build was not byte-identical.
what_is_missing: A standing 'no change without a logged decision' rule, and a durable byte-identity check.
options: A) Keep the dated log and fix drift as it is found. B) Add a byte-identity check to CI. C) Leave it.
recommendation: A and B. The drift found today is repaired in this build; a CI byte-identity check is the durable fix.
blocks: Whether 'a clean build reproduces the published numbers' stays true.
